sourceNote: Mineral identity and Mohs hardness are facts. 'modernAssociations' are modern crystal-practice beliefs with no demonstrated physical effects, and they are labelled as such in the UI. In this game, stones are used as tactile grounding anchors: weight, temperature and texture. Ethical sourcing varies widely; second-hand or known-origin stones are better.

crystals.name: Hematite
crystals.tactile: Surprisingly heavy for its size, cool to the touch, and glassy smooth. A very good stone for 'feel the weight in your palm'.
safetyNotes: Strongly magnetic 'hematite' jewellery is usually a synthetic called hematine. Keep it away from pacemakers and bank cards.

crystals.name: Smoky quartz
crystals.tactile: Cool, hard and glassy. Translucent browns and greys, like looking through woodsmoke.
careNotes: Much commercial smoky quartz is artificially irradiated clear quartz.

crystals.name: Clear quartz
crystals.tactile: Hard, cold at first, and slowly warming in your hand. Rainbows appear where it's fractured inside.
careNotes: Can focus sunlight like a lens. Don't leave it in a sunny window near fabric.

crystals.name: Amethyst
crystals.mineral: Quartz (SiO₂), purple from iron and natural irradiation
crystals.tactile: Faceted points with sharp-ish edges, or smooth when tumbled. Purple deepens toward the tips.

crystals.name: Rose quartz
crystals.tactile: Milky, soft pink, and usually tumbled very smooth. Pleasant to rub with your thumb.

crystals.name: Black tourmaline (schorl)
crystals.tactile: Long, striated ridges run along its length, so you can feel the grooves under your fingernail.
careNotes: Brittle across its length. Raw pieces can splinter.

crystals.name: Moonstone
crystals.tactile: Smooth and pearly, with a bluish glow (adularescence) that floats across the surface as you tilt it.
careNotes: Has cleavage planes, so it can crack if knocked.

crystals.name: Labradorite
crystals.tactile: Dull grey until it catches the light just right, then flashes of blue, green and gold appear. Good for an 'I'll notice when it changes' focus exercise.

crystals.name: Carnelian
crystals.tactile: Waxy and warm-looking, in translucent orange-red. It glows like an ember against light.
careNotes: Much commercial carnelian is heat-treated or dyed agate.

crystals.name: Obsidian
crystals.tactile: Glass-smooth and black, with a mirror-like shine when polished.
safetyNotes: Broken or raw obsidian has edges sharper than a scalpel. Only handle tumbled pieces.

crystals.name: Selenite
crystals.tactile: Silky, fibrous and soft enough to scratch with a fingernail. Feels faintly warm compared with quartz.
careNotes: Water damages it: it dissolves and pits. Never wash or soak it.
Most stones sold as 'selenite' are the fibrous variety, satin spar.

crystals.name: Malachite
crystals.tactile: Banded swirls of deep and light green, like rings in a cut tree. Polished pieces are cool and silky.
careNotes: Soft, so it scratches easily. Keep away from acids and household cleaners.
safetyNotes: Dust from cutting or sanding is toxic. Never make 'gem elixirs' or put it in drinks. Wash your hands after handling raw pieces.

crystals.name: Tiger's eye
crystals.tactile: Golden-brown bands shimmer and roll as you turn it (chatoyancy), like light on water.
safetyNotes: Polished stones are safe to handle, but they should never be cut or ground at home, because the original fibres were a form of asbestos.
